headline: Learned models map nuclear export, protein localization, and endocytic carrier dynamics
label: Experimentally Constrained Structure Modeling
summary: Recent preprints apply AlphaFold 3 at proteome scale and morphology-aware deep learning to live-cell trafficking data.
synthesis: The three preprints apply deep-learning models to the spatial organization of proteins and membrane carriers. The XPO1 study uses AlphaFold 3 to model cargo-XPO1-RanGTP complexes for over 4,000 human proteins, producing a proteome-scale atlas of nuclear export sequences. DualLoc fine-tunes cascaded dual transformers on protein language models to predict multi-compartment subcellular localization. Shape2Fate tracks exo- and endocytic carriers in live-cell TIRF-SIM movies with a morphology-aware pipeline, with pathway-specific readouts. The dominant thread is learned models producing compartment-level or trafficking-relevant outputs at scale. Only Shape2Fate is directly anchored to experimental imaging data, so the shared element is not a common data modality. What is new is the coupling of predictive models to subcellular-scale outputs, from nuclear export sequences to localization classes and carrier trajectories.
